title: Student and early-career AI game devs: what have you actually shipped?
author: lollyadorable4
selftext:
I’m 23 and I keep wondering how many people around my gen are already using AI to build and actually finish games.  
If you’re a student, early in your career, or building games on the side, share what you’re working on, how far you’ve taken it and what your process has been like.

I’d especially love to hear from Women creators working in this space. I don’t see many tbh, and I think it’s important!  
What has AI genuinely helped you with, and what parts are you still handling yourself? Share your game if it has grown beyond the first prompt or experiment into something people can actually play :)))

comments.author: lollyadorable4
comments.body: Omg so many comments Ill try to respond everyone!!!! Lol

comments.author: business_warrior
comments.body:
Released 3 android games, one 1k+ downloads, the other one is 500 downloads.

Games are very stable, I test and do bug fix. So far made like 35 dollars. 25 from ads, 10 from in game purchases.

Crash rate is 0.64%, very low.

—-

Games are built using Unity + MCP server connected to Claude Code. 3D assets are purchased from asset store. For UI I used Claude Design.

replies.author: lollyadorable4
replies.body:
I haven’t seen many people connect Claude Code to Unity through an MCP server yet. How much can Claude do directly inside Unity with that setup?  
Also, I’d love to check out the games if you’re comfortable sharing the links :) Are you building them alongside university/work, or working on games full-time?

replies.author: business_warrior
replies.body:
I won’t share my projects. Yea, I was doing that alongside full time work. 

Claude can do everything with MCP, it basically allows Claude to “see” the UI of the unity. The one I used is by Ivan Murzak, search him up on YouTube.

comments.author: Gh0st3d
comments.body:
Released a mobile card game "Cards of Myth" (https://www.cardsofmyth.com) 

Mix of paid assets, free assets, and generated assets. AI helped me feel motivated because artwork is always a huge road block for me. It also helped me build tools on the side to help assess card balance, which I could then use to plan new cards. Finally, obviously helped me code faster. 

I stuck with the languages I knew so I could move relatively fast since my game is a mostly "2d" game, I didn't bother getting familiar with a game engine. And with that, AI also helped refine performance to milk out every bit of FPS I could with javascript / css powered graphics.

replies.author: lollyadorable4
replies.body: WOW those numbers are seriously impressive!! What game is it, and where did AI fit into the development process?
